title: Signature-baseline suite and adaptive workload sampler for kernel routing CI
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem: CI perf gates and golden baselines frequently fluctuate because the current workload selection is brittle to small shifts in traffic composition and prefill state. This leads to noisy p50/p95/p99 signals and a high false-positive rate for regressions.

Goal: Build a signature-baseline suite that captures compact fingerprints of workload + prefill state and an adaptive sampler that selects a small, bounded set of traces for deterministic CI runs. The sampler should prioritize coverage of kernel-routing-relevant dimensions (prefill lengths, KV cache hit patterns, attention window usage, batching distribution) and be cheap enough to run in nightly and presubmit CI.

Outcomes: reduce CI false-positive perf regressions by >=45%, keep nightly run budget <= 120 GPU-minutes, and provide trace-level explainability for gate failures.
acceptance_criteria: A signature schema defined that encodes: prefill_len histogram bucket, avg_kv_hit_ratio, max_attention_window, batch_size_dist, model_variant_tag, and kernel_variant_hint.
An adaptive sampler implementation that selects <= 80 traces for a CI run while maximizing coverage across signature buckets (measured via Jaccard coverage >= 0.85 vs full corpus).
Deterministic seeding for golden runs; CI job artifacts contain seed and full signature mapping for reproducibility.
Nightly CI job completes within 120 GPU-minutes on the dedicated bench pool and produces a stable baseline artifact stored in artifacts/runtime-signatures/<date>.
Dashboard panels for signature drift and per-signature latency deltas added to the runtime-benchboard; runbook for triage of CI gate failures linked.
Integration tests that validate sampler preserves p99 behavior within +/-5% compared to full-run on three representative models.
Documentation (Confluence) and example CLI to generate signature files from trace captures.
Performance gate thresholds adjusted and test-vectorized so presubmit runs fail only when signature cohort deltas exceed configured SLOs.
implementation_notes: Signature generation happens during trace postprocessing: add a lightweight pass that computes required aggregates and writes a compact JSON line per trace.
Sampler uses stratified reservoir sampling across discretized buckets; bucket weights derived from production traffic distribution snapshots stored in telemetry.

Keep kernel-routing signals as advisory metadata — sampler should prefer diversity of kernel hints but not hard-fix kernel selection for CI runs to avoid conflating runtime optimizer changes with workload shift.
Provide a small compatibility shim so legacy golden-run consumers can read signature artifacts (export map: signature_hash -> trace_id).
Implement GPU warmup and KV-cache priming steps in the CI job to reduce prefill cold-start noise; make these toggles configurable per signature.
Expose sampler knobs (target_size, seed, bucket_weights) through the bench CLI and CI job templates for rapid experimentation.
testing_plan: Unit tests for signature extractor and sampler determinism (seeded runs produce identical signature sets).
Backfill sampler results against a 5k-trace offline corpus; compute coverage and p99 delta metrics and store as CSV artifacts.
Run A/B: nightly full-corpus run vs sampler-run for 14 days to measure gate stability improvement and variance reduction on p95/p99.
Stress test sampler with synthetic skewed distributions (heavy tail in prefill lengths and batch sizes) to ensure worst-case coverage degrades gracefully.
Presubmit smoke: run a 20-trace sampler job on PRs touching kernel-routing code paths to catch regressions faster with low cost.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Sampler misses rare-but-critical traces that trigger regressions. Mitigation: include an explicit 'rare' bucket from production telemetry and periodically run full-corpus goldenization weekly.
Risk: Signature schema evolves and breaks historical baselines. Mitigation: version signature schema and provide migration tooling to recompute prior artifacts on demand.
Risk: Added CI warmup increases runtime and cost. Mitigation: make warmup optional per-signature and tune warmup lengths to the minimum required for stable cache state.
Risk: Overfitting to current kernel-routing heuristics. Mitigation: keep kernel_hint advisory and maintain a separate canonical run that pins kernels to validate optimizer changes.
